samples.question: The picture shows a pin board of ten grey switches arranged in four rows of one, two, three and four, and five coloured bins in a row along the bottom. Each switch is a square grey block with a short grey tongue sticking out of its left side or out of its right side. The dark blue discs on the shelf at the top are the balls to be released: there are as many balls as discs, and they are released one at a time, each one finishing its whole fall before the next one is released. Every ball starts at the single switch of the top row. When a ball reaches a switch it leaves that switch towards the side its tongue is sticking out of at that moment, and it then arrives at the switch of the next row down that lies on that side: a tongue on the right sends the ball to the next lower switch to its lower right, and a tongue on the left sends it to the next lower switch to its lower left. Immediately after a ball has left a switch, that switch throws its tongue over to its other side, so the next ball that reaches the same switch is sent the opposite way, the ball after that is sent the original way again, and so on. Switches that no ball reaches keep the tongue drawn in the picture. Below the bottom row of switches there are five exit slots, and each coloured bin sits directly under one exit slot, as the faint grey guide lines show; a ball that leaves the bottom row falls into the bin under the slot it left from. The tongues are drawn as they stand before any ball is released, and no later position of any ball or tongue is drawn anywhere. Into which coloured bin does the last released ball fall? Answer with one colour word: red, green, yellow, orange or purple.
